paper.title_en: Impact of the Initial Lorentz Factor on Kinetic Instabilities, Magnetic-Field Evolution, and Particle Acceleration in Relativistic Jets
paper.abstract_en: We investigate how the initial Lorentz factor shapes the evolution of relativistic jets---a key open question in high-energy astrophysics. Using global three-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations with cylindrical jet geometry on a Cartesian grid, we analyze the self-consistent evolution of relativistic electron--positron and electron--ion jets from active galactic nuclei (AGN) and their interaction with the ambient medium. We implement an injection scheme that assigns space- and time-dependent velocities to injected particles and simulate jets with initial Lorentz factors of $γ_{0} = 10$ and 15. Jets with the higher Lorentz factor ($γ_{0} = 15$) exhibit stronger electron collimation, whereas those with $γ_{0} = 10$ show larger growth rates of kinetic instabilities during the linear stage. In both cases, a non-oscillatory electric field accelerates and decelerates charged particles throughout the linear and nonlinear stages. Upon entering the nonlinear regime, the initial toroidal magnetic field undergoes significant amplification driven by the Weibel instability (WI), the kinetic Kelvin--Helmholtz instability (kKHI), and the mushroom instability (MI), and subsequently reorganizes into complex topologies. In the late nonlinear stage, magnetic islands with randomly swirling fields indicate a highly turbulent magnetic structure. These findings demonstrate that global 3D~PIC modeling is essential for capturing the interplay among kinetic instabilities, magnetic turbulence, and particle acceleration in relativistic outflows, bridging microscopic plasma physics with macroscopic observations of AGN jets and gamma-ray bursts.
